verdict.rationale: Reducto documents an async parse endpoint (`run_job()` / POST /parse_async) that returns a job ID immediately. It also documents Svix webhooks with cryptographic signing, retries with exponential backoff, and a delivery dashboard, which covers the non-blocking submit and the callback parts of the story. missing for 10: explicit documentation of a job-status polling endpoint, explicit confirmation that webhooks fire on parse-job completion, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, long parses run as async jobs with status polling and completion webhooks, so my pipeline never blocks

citations.quote: `run_job()` Calls async endpoint, returns job ID
Svix webhooks provide cryptographic request signing, automatic retries with exponential backoff, and a delivery dashboard for debugging. Use Svix for production applications.
In Reducto Studio, go to Webhooks in the sidebar. This opens your Svix dashboard directly.
